candidates.lead: Rap fans say people were "choking" and "coughing up blood" towards the end of Don Toliver's gig
candidates.evidence_text: Police look for more than 100 gig-goers to help Co-op Live investigation - BBC News Image caption, More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from the arena during the rapper's concert By Stewart Whittingham and Rachael Lazaro , North West Published 27 November 2026 Police have said they are trying to contact more than 100 gig-goers to help their investigation after an unknown substance was released at a concert at Manchester's Co-op Live arena. Detectives believe a "small group of organised criminals targeted people in the crowd to commit a series of robberies on the night". More than 12,000 people were evacuated from the arena during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver on Sunday. One woman was taken to hospital and 88 others were treated at the scene after concertgoers reported a "horrible smell" and some people "coughing up blood". No arrests have been made and the substance has not yet been identified. Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said: "We're working to identify those [robbery] suspects and the substance that we believe was released in the crowd as part of these incidents. "All of this work is ongoing at pace. He said there had been "similar incidents at two Don Toliver gigs in Europe that are also relevant to our enquiries". Fans reported that a spray or gas was released into the crowd in Zurich and Paris. Image source, Handout Image caption, Fans say they were in quarantine at the Etihad sports hall for about six hours Jess Kinyata, 20, from West London, who was one of 12,000 people evacuated from the arena, said before the "gas began" his 18 carat gold chain, worth about £1,500, was stolen from him during a set by the concert's opening artist, Victony. GMP previously said there had been nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert. Harding said officers had been "working through footage captured on mobile phones and CCTV". He added: "There are over a hundred people at the gig that we are working to try and contact to potentially assist with our enquiries. "We thank all those that have assisted us so far. "We also know many more people were impacted on the night and afterwards, physically and psychologically." To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, Joey Howe said there was confusion and panic when the show stopped North West Ambulance Service said it had deployed crews, including its Hazardous Area Response Team, who carried out decontamination "as a precaution". Those who suffered symptoms had been taken to the Etihad stadium. Some fans complained the process, which involved them changing into paper white suits and putting their clothes in a plastic bag, was "invasive" and "traumatic". Many stayed quarantined for several hours before being able to leave in the early hours of Monday. GMP said: "People's safety, and the safety of the wider community, was at the forefront of officers' minds throughout." Image source, Press Association Image caption, Fans said the incident happened 30 to 40 minutes into the rapper's set The substance was released at about 22:00 GMT, near the end of Toliver's show as part of his Nitrous – Octane world tour. Concertgoers have described feeling "unsafe" and seeing "distressing" scenes and people "coughing up blood". Posting on Instagram, Toliver said: "My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured. "The only thing I love more than creating music is performing for my fans." Co-op Live, which reopened its doors on Thursday night for a gig by American singer Phoebe Bridgers, previously said its priority remained "the safety and security of all visitors" to the venue. You can also send story ideas via Whatsapp to 0808 100 2230. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Catherine, Princess of Wales has become the patron of The Christie hospital in Manchester, describing it as an "extraordinary place" The princess, a former cancer patient, said she was "delighted" to become the figurehead of the leading cancer treatment hospital and The Christie Charity after visiting its Withington site in June Her cancer journey is the subject of a new documentary called Heal, which features the her saying how being "faced with your own mortality" meant accepting life is not infinite which "softens your heart" In a social media post, the she wrote: "During my visit to The Christie NHS Foundation Trust, I saw first-hand how exceptional care extends beyond treatment alone "When people face serious illness, it is often the compassion, relationships and support that surround them which help sustain hope and resilience through the most challenging times "The Christie's commitment to caring for the whole person, alongside it's world-leading clinical expertise, makes it an extraordinary place

candidates.evidence_text: Tributes to veteran killed after being hit by car in Swinton - BBC News Image source, Greater Manchester Police Image caption, Terry Hutchinson died on 22 November after being hit by a car Published 27 November 2026 The family of a "proud military veteran" who died after being hit by a car has paid tribute to him. Terry Hutchinson, 88, was struck on Station Road in Swinton at 18:09 GMT on 22 November and was pronounced dead at the scene. A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and has been bailed pending further investigation. Paying tribute to a "much-loved" husband, brother, uncle, dad, grandad and great-grandad, his family said: "Terry was a proud military veteran who served his country with pride." They continued: "Despite his age, he continued to enjoy an active and healthy lifestyle. Having worked hard throughout his life, Terry carried that same determination and spirit into his retirement years." Describing him as a "kind and thoughtful gentleman", they said he "touched the lives of those around him and will be fondly remembered, deeply missed and forever cherished by his family, friends and all who knew and loved him". A GMP spokesman added: "Our focus on the evening was safely evacuating 12,000 people and supporting emergency services colleagues as they managed the decontamination process, involving an unknown substance." The force has not confirmed what the substance was and there have been no arrests

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Some Don Toliver fans who were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live arena after an unknown substance was released have said they were "quarantined for six hours" and threatened with arrest if they did not remove all their clothing Jordan, 33, from Scotland, said he and his brothers were among 88 people who were taken for decontamination after the incident at the gig on Sunday night , and it "felt like I was being taken hostage" and was "so traumatic" He said they had asked for medical help at 22:15 GMT and were taken to the Etihad Stadium and made to change into paper suits, before being released at about 04:45 on Monday Greater Manchester Police said: "People's safety, and the safety of the wider community, was at the forefront of officers' minds throughout." A GMP spokesman added: "Our focus on the evening was safely evacuating 12,000 people and supporting emergency services colleagues as they managed the decontamination process, involving an unknown substance." The force has not confirmed what the substance was and there have been no arrests

candidates.lead: The prime minister vowed to get people off the streets by Christmas when he entered Downing Street
candidates.evidence_text: A homeless charity's co-founder has said he fears Andy Burnham will not be able to meet his pledge to end rough sleeping as the number of those sleeping on the streets in Manchester continues to rise When he entered Downing Street in the summer, the prime minister pledged to provide a route out of rough sleeping by Christmas through a £442m package of emergency accommodation and practical support over three years A further £432m was added to the scheme in October However, with just weeks to go until Christmas, Dave Evans, from the Two Brews charity, said he believed rough sleeping had "gone up dramatically" as he witnessed the daily struggle of those on the streets When Burnham was first elected as the Mayor of Greater Manchester in May 2017, he made the same pledge to end the need for rough sleeping across all 10 boroughs He made a great start with the number of rough sleepers in Greater Manchester reducing during the pandemic to 89 in 2021 from 268 in 2017

In fact it was a bit more than that When Ms Lawal's luggage was searched as she returned from Nigeria almost 60,000 Benson & Hedges were discovered, a court heard . The cigs were around 300 times the traveller's allowance and had an estimated retail value of more than £45,000 The amount of excise duty, customs duty and import VAT evaded was later calculated as £37,757 and Ms Lawal was ordered to pay a £15,102 penalty. But the case ended up in court when Ms Lawal, said to be a single mum bringing up four children on Universal Credit, appealed against t At a remote hearing of the first tier tribunal tax chamber, she claimed she 'intended to approach a Border Force officer of her own accord and disclose that she was carrying the cigarettes'. She said Border Force officer Sonny Bailey approached her after she collected her suitcas But Mr Bailey disputed that version of events. He told the court he stopped Ms Lawal when she entered the green 'Nothing to declare' lane after she arrived at Manchester Airport via Doha on July 5, 2024. candidates.lead: Manchester Nearly 90 per cent voters in Harpurhey turned their back on this week’s by-election – we asked some why?
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Nearly 90 per cent voters in Harpurhey turned their back on this week’s by-election – we asked some why? The poll, won by Labour after the recent death of Coun Pat Karney, saw apathy reign on the streets of North Manchester Add to preferred Labour triumphed in the Harpurhey by-election on Thursday with Labour’s Abdul Sarfraz, 26, winning the race The vote was triggered after the death of former councillor Pat Karney last month, aged 78. He was one of Manchester’s most recognised faces, who served the area for nearly 50 years Coun Sarfraz, who described Pat Karney as a ‘mentor’, won the election comfortably, picking up 1,016 votes, ahead of Reform UK’s candidate Ian Carter in second with 366 It was a comfortable victory in an area where Labour have grown used to winning. But there was one extremely striking feature of the by-election An exceptionally low turnout saw just 12.9 per cent of eligible voters in the ward casting a ballot at the polls. In May this year when local elections were last held, the turnout in Harpurhey was the lowest for any ward in Manchester at 22.35 per cent

Jake, 31, has now spoken of his devastating loss, describing Sophie as the 'greatest' mum and 'the woman who gave him the best five years of his life' The couple had been together for five years, they got engaged at midnight on New Year's Day and had been looking forward to building their future together as a family with the recent addition of their little girl Rosie. Following the devastating loss, Jake is determined to make s In a heartbreaking tribute, Jake said: "I just hope you know how much you were loved by those closest around you, we miss you every moment of every day since. I'm so sorry you only got to be a mummy for six weeks as I know how excited you were to become one and how much it meant "I promise I will always love and remember you and I promise I will make you proud every single day I walk this earth. candidates.lead: Manchester Nearly 90 per cent voters in Harpurhey turned their back on this week’s by-election – we asked some why?
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Nearly 90 per cent voters in Harpurhey turned their back on this week’s by-election – we asked some why? The poll, won by Labour after the recent death of Coun Pat Karney, saw apathy reign on the streets of North Manchester Add to preferred Labour triumphed in the Harpurhey by-election on Thursday with Labour’s Abdul Sarfraz, 26, winning the race The vote was triggered after the death of former councillor Pat Karney last month, aged 78. He was one of Manchester’s most recognised faces, who served the area for nearly 50 years Coun Sarfraz, who described Pat Karney as a ‘mentor’, won the election comfortably, picking up 1,016 votes, ahead of Reform UK’s candidate Ian Carter in second with 366 It was a comfortable victory in an area where Labour have grown used to winning. But there was one extremely striking feature of the by-election An exceptionally low turnout saw just 12.9 per cent of eligible voters in the ward casting a ballot at the polls. In May this year when local elections were last held, the turnout in Harpurhey was the lowest for any ward in Manchester at 22.35 per cent

candidates.evidence_text: Dear readers, we're just getting started… As MEN Premium marks its first anniversary, editor-in-chief Sarah Lester reflects on a changing world for local journalism, the importance of telling Greater Manchester's story and the 7,000 readers who have c Add to preferred sources News Sarah Lester 12:32, 27 Nov 2026 Updated 12:33, 27 Nov 2026 I’ve been a journalist for a long time I love stories and storytelling, I love investigations, I love finding out what’s really going on and telling our readers. It’s what the Manchester Evening News has always done. And it’s more important now than ever When I started at the Manchester Evening News we had five print editions a day. We filed stories from our notepads over the phone to people called copytakers Now, through our website and social media, our journalism reaches numbers of people past editors could only have dreamt of About a year ago we tried something different. We introduced Premium, putting some of our stories behind a paywall. We also limited the number of stories people could read for free, while keeping breaking news free to everyone

Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter A Salford councillor is giving locals a ‘gift’ in the run up to Christmas . Residents in Eccles will benefit from free parking at the area’s seven car parks on the three Saturdays leading up to the festive period The move will save residents a ‘small amount of money in the run up to the most expensive time of year’, according to local councillor Mike McCusker. The scheme applies to seven council-run car parks in Eccles, Monton, and Swinton , which are on Hankinson Way, John William Street The scheme is also geared at supporting local businesses, with the hope that locals might make use of their highstreet offers instead of ordering all their Christmas shopping online Councillor McCusker, who represents Eccles, said: “We’ve got a gift for you in the seven car parks that Salford City Council runs. You can get free parking on the free Saturdays leading up to Christmas. It will help you save a small amount of money at this expensive time of year. He added: “We’re delighted to bring back free festive parking this Christmas, helping residents save a little extra money at what can be an expensive time of year, while giving our local businesses a welcome boost

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford The ‘gift’ a Salford councillor is giving his residents in the run up to Christmas It will save residents around £3.50 - but it's a commitment to local businesses. Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter A Salford councillor is giving locals a ‘gift’ in the run up to Christmas . Residents in Eccles will benefit from free parking at the area’s seven car parks on the three Saturdays leading up to the festive period The move will save residents a ‘small amount of money in the run up to the most expensive time of year’, according to local councillor Mike McCusker. The scheme applies to seven council-run car parks in Eccles, Monton, and Swinton , which are on Hankinson Way, John William Street The scheme is also geared at supporting local businesses, with the hope that locals might make use of their highstreet offers instead of ordering all their Christmas shopping online Councillor McCusker, who represents Eccles, said: “We’ve got a gift for you in the seven car parks that Salford City Council runs. You can get free parking on the free Saturdays leading up to Christmas. It will help you save a small amount of money at this expensive time of year. He added: “We’re delighted to bring back free festive parking this Christmas, helping residents save a little extra money at what can be an expensive time of year, while giving our local businesses a welcome boost

candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 10:33am Kirith Entwistle, the Labour MP for Bolton North East, has said she found the current court system "triggering" and had to watch her abuser "stare at her". Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

candidates.evidence_text: Tuesday 6 October 2026 at 5:15pm Zac Bolland and and his accomplice David Worrall were both given four life sentences for the petrol bombing. Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

A Don Toliver fan who was evacuated from a concert in Manchester has said his gold necklace was ripped from his neck in the "chaotic" mosh pit Jess Kinyata, 20, from West London, was one of 12,000 people to be evacuated from the Co-op Live arena after an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd He said before the "gas began" his 18 carat gold chain, worth about £1,500, was stolen from him during a set by the concert's opening artist, Victony Greater Manchester Police said there have been nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert. No arrests have yet been made and the substance has not yet been identified In a statement released on Friday, the force said it had tried to contact more than 100 gig-goers to help the investigation Adding it suspected a "small group of organised criminals targeted people in the crowd to commit a series of robberies on the night"

candidates.lead: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund
candidates.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Council has set out how it will continue providing vital frontline services despite the ongoing financial challenges facing local authorities across the UK The council has published its budget for 2027/28 reflecting many of these challenges, including continued demand on social care, pressures from rising prices and geopolitical events causing economic uncertainty The budget will now be considered at a meeting of the council’s cabinet on 7 th December. If approved the draft proposals will be subject to a full public consultation The Local Government Association (LGA) Corporate Peer Challenge review in 2025 found that Bolton was in a stronger financial position relative to other local authorities However, the budget makes clear that some difficult decisions will still be needed to protect essential frontline services The report details the requirement to make £9.1m of savings in 2027/28, with indications of the likely further savings required in future financial years

candidates.evidence_text: A full day of festive fun, family experiences, and entertainment will bring Christmas magic to the heart of Bolton on Thursday 3rd December Market Place Bolton is set to bring festive cheer to the town this December with ‘A Day of Christmas Magic’ - a fun filled day boasting a packed programme of Christmas experiences, entertainment, and seasonal activities for all ages On Thursday 3rd December, from 11am to 8pm, the event will transform Market Place into a destination for festive fun throughout the day, bringing together families, friends, and the wider Bolton community to celebrate the magic of Christmas There will be something for everyone, as the centre offers a variety of family-friendly activities, seasonal entertainment, and opportunities to make some very special Christmas memories Younger visitors and families can enjoy daytime Christmas activities from The Light, including baby-friendly experiences, alongside Christmas crafts, appearances from Mrs Claus and her elves, and the chance to enjoy Santa Live The day will also feature local theatre and pantomime partners, with supporting entertainment adding to the atmosphere throughout the event

It provides advice and support on cost-of-living pressures, heating and fuel costs, food As part of the programme, 500 Winter Well packs are being distributed to older and more vulnerable residents across the borough. candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Mon 30th Nov, 2026 - Stray A WHYTE Christmas with Stray and Whyte Rushen Stray, Eagle St, Manchester M4 5BU Mon 30th Nov, 2026 6.30pm Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Christmas dinner is getting a radical rethink on Monday 30 November, as WHYTE’S returns to Manchester for a one-night-only takeover with Stray , marking the return of the cocktail bar’s Long Table dinner series Following their pop-up in 2025, Whyte Rushen and Liv Akers are back, with the main hall of Mackie Mayor transformed into a candlelit dining room for just 40 guests The WHYTE’S team has spent the past 18 months travelling the world, hosting more than 55 international events and creating menus informed by the ingredients and food cultures of the places they visit. For their return to Manchester, they’re putting their own spin on the British C Things start with fried brioche, stem ginger butter and pickled Brussels sprouts, followed by a raw hand-dived XL scallop cocktail with fresh apple, trout roe and bottarga, and aged beef tartare with brown crab and horseradish dressing, duck yolk and roast potatoes Then there’s pan-fried house stuffing loaf with bread sauce and three-meat gravy, triple-cooked turkey leg with blue cheese, cranberry and port, and a mince pie crumble with brandy custard and salted beef fat caramel

candidates.lead: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre […] The post Sona Jobarteh Tour appeared first on Band on the Wall
candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

The new office quadruples capacity at the bank’s Northern headquarters, and supports the bank’s ambitions to double the number of roles in Manchester in the coming years, including technical roles in product engineering. The move strengthens Allica’s presence in the North, where Greater Manchester alone is home to almost 24,000 established businesses. Allica Bank, the leading fintech bank for established businesses, has today opened a significantly larger office in central Manchester as it continues to grow its presence in the North of England. The office was opened today by the Mayor of Greater Manchester, Bev Craig, and follows a period of rapid growth for Allica – the UK’s fastest growing fintech in history, which has increased its headcount by over 80% since the end of 2023. The new office – located at the gateway to Manchester’s innovation district on Oxford Road – allows Allica to quadruple the number of desks in the City from 8 to 32, giving its growing Manchester team significantly more space to work together in the office. It will also support Allica’s ambitions to double the size of its team in Manchester in the coming years, with it expecting to create 60 new roles across a range of teams, including technical roles in the bank’s product engineering teams and customer relationship managers. The larger office and expanded team in Manchester will underpin Allica’s plans to accelerate its lending to established businesses in the UK. Allica has already lent over £4 billion since getting its banking licence in 2019 and plans to lend well over £2 billion to established businesses in 2027 alone. These businesses, typically employing between five and 250 people, are a vital part of the national and regional economy. Greater Manchester alone is home to an estimated 24,000 established businesses employing 453,000 people, including 113,000 in the city of Manchester itself. Typically underserved by the big banks, Allica is providing access to finance for these businesses through a combination of human relationships and proprietary AI technology. Allica’s lending in 2025 alone supported over 12,000 jobs in the North West and contributed £870 million to the region’s GDP. Located at the heart of Manchester’s City Centre, the new office is on the doorstep to the Oxford Road Corridor, the City’s innovation district and home to a concentrated number of businesses, research facilities and creative industries. The building itself is a recently redeveloped textile and shipping warehouse dating back to 1886, meaning that a building that once served Manchester’s merchants now houses a bank built solely for the established businesses that drive the UK’s economy today. Richard Davies, CEO of Allica Bank , said, “Manchester has always been a city of ambitious businesses and we are proud that Allica can be a part of its next chapter. Our new office gives the growing team more space to do their best work, and in a building with some real Manchester history. “Allica has grown rapidly over the last few years and as we grow we want to invest in places with talent and ambition. Manchester is exactly that kind of city, and we have big plans for our team here and our commitment to the North in the long-term.” Bev Craig, Mayor of Greater Manchester, said: “We want Greater Manchester to be a place where businesses can grow, invest and create good jobs for people here, with good growth supported by the skills, finance and support businesses need to succeed. “Allica’s expansion will create 60 new jobs in Manchester, including in technology and engineering, alongside its work providing finance to businesses across the region. It’s a welcome investment in Greater Manchester and in the people and businesses behind its growth.” Joe Manning, Managing Director of Invest Manchester, said: “Allica’s growth in Manchester is great news for our financial and professional services sector, which employs more than 326,000 people across Greater Manchester. In August, Nothing Gold Can Stay took Robert Frost’s poem about transience as its starting point. Where that show dwelt on things passing, this one is more interested in what lasts The four contributing artists each approach time differently, thinking about how the past and the future shape the way ideas are understood. Anna Clough, a Cumbrian-born artist based at Salford’s Paradise Works, has made walking performances tracing mining landscapes from the Neo Sheffield’s Charlotte Dawson treats everyday objects – souvenirs, collections – as vessels for memory. Olivia England, who graduated from Manchester School of Art alongside Clough, reworks found objects, text and imagery through bookbinding and print, while London-based Elliot Fo Seeing the work from a perspective that isn’t your own is meant to open up conversations about the legacy of ideas, collective memory and what our actions leave behind for people we’ll never meet

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Japanese restaurant will form part of Manchester’s tallest building, with an opening pencilled in for 2032… Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Luxury Japanese restaurant and hotel brand Nobu has released new CGI images of its forthcoming Manchester restaurant, offering a glimpse of what diners can expect when it opens in 2032 The restaurant will form part of the 76-storey Viadux 2 development, located between Deansgate Locks and Manchester Central, which is set to become the city’s tallest building Founded by chef Nobu Matsuhisa, actor Robert De Niro and film producer Meir Teper, Nobu has become synonymous with contemporary Japanese dining, blending traditional Japanese cooking with Peruvian influences Its signature dishes include black cod with miso, yellowtail sashimi with jalapeño and rock shrimp tempura, which have become staples of its restaurants around the world Plans for the Manchester development were first revealed in March 2025, with Nobu taking on a significant presence within the skyscraper. Alongside the restaurant, there will be a 160-room five-star hotel and 452 luxury branded residences

candidates.evidence_text: Food & Drink Bars Loungers to open Fosforo Lounge in Stretford on Saturday 28th November . . Food & Drink . Bars . Openings . Loungers to open Fosforo Lounge in Stretford on Saturday 28th November. By. About Manchester - . . November 9, 2026 0 . . . . . . Facebook. . Twitter. . Google+. . Pinterest. . WhatsApp. . . . . . Cadno Lounge, Neath . Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. Becoming a genuine part of the community is incredibly important to us, and we can’t wait to meet our neighbours and get involved locally.. . “If you’re looking for a friendly, flexible space for events or group meet‑ups, pop in once we’re open – we’d love to chat and see how we can help.”. . . . . . . candidates.evidence_text: The Manchester charity plans to deliver more than 27,000 chef-made meals a year from its new headquarters… Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Manchester food charity Eat Well MCR has opened its new permanent home in Mayfield Park, taking over two of the historic railway arches at Depot Mayfield The new headquarters, officially launched on Wednesday evening (25 November), gives the charity its own dedicated kitchen, allowing it to feed thousands more people across Greater Manchester and expand its work with disadvantaged young people Eat Well MCR was born out of the pandemic in March 2020, when chef Mary-Ellen McTague was forced to close her Chorlton restaurant and turned her attention to cooking meals for NHS workers, establishing the initiative alongside Kathleen O’Connor and Gemma Saunders Since then, it has delivered more than 175,000 chef-made meals to people experiencing difficult circumstances, from families living in temporary accommodation and women seeking refuge to families with seriously ill children staying at Ronald McDonald House It has become a collective of some of Manchester’s best-known restaurants and chefs, with the likes of Hawksmoor, Hello Oriental, Maray and Dishoom all contributing to its meal provision

candidates.evidence_text: Counter Manchester , the much-anticipated new restaurant from Open Restaurant Group , opens its doors today at 12pm. It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander
